title: Intro — Application Security
summary: Web apps = client, server, database. Almost every web vuln is untrusted input reaching a dangerous sink. Golden rule: never trust client input.
objectives: Read the client -> server -> sink flow.
Learn the golden rule about client input.
task: Should you TRUST data coming from the client? Answer true or false.
hint: The attacker controls the request, so never.

title: Web & APIs — Fundamentals
summary: HTTP = method, path, headers, body. Server reads inputs (source) and passes them to a sink. APIs exchange JSON with a bearer token.
objectives: Learn request parts and status codes.
curl a site with -D - and read the headers.
task: What do we call the dangerous operation that untrusted input reaches? (one word)

title: Access Control — Broken Access Control (A01)
summary: The #1 web risk: reaching data/actions you shouldn't. IDOR = object returned by id with no ownership check.
objectives: Understand why UI-hiding is not a control.
task: What is the common abbreviation for Insecure Direct Object Reference?

title: Injection — SQL & Command (A03)
summary: Untrusted input becomes part of a command/query the server runs. SQLi and command injection.
objectives: Run the SQLi and command-injection exploits.
task: What kind of SQL queries prevent injection? (one word, spelled 'parameterized')
hint: Data travels separately from the query.

title: XSS — Cross-Site Scripting (A03)
summary: Your input echoed into HTML runs as code in a victim's browser. Fix: output encoding + CSP.
task: What is the 3-letter abbreviation for this vulnerability?

title: SSRF — Server-Side Request Forgery (A10)
summary: You make the server fetch internal URLs, e.g. the cloud metadata IP 169.254.169.254. Fix: block private/loopback/link-local ranges.
objectives: Use SSRF to read a local file.
task: 169.254.169.254 belongs to which reserved IP range? (one hyphenated word)
hint: Same range your network training calls 169.254.0.0/16.

title: Auth — Authentication & JWT (A07)
summary: Forge-able tokens = account takeover. Fix: random server-side sessions. JWT classic flaw: accepting alg:none.
task: A JWT whose header alg is set to ___ has no signature and must be rejected.

title: Crypto — Cryptographic Failures (A02)
summary: Weak hashing and leaked secrets. Passwords need salted slow hashes; secrets live in env vars or a vault, never in code.
objectives: See why MD5 password hashes are unsafe.
task: Secrets like API keys should live in environment variables or a ___ (one word).

title: Deserialization — Insecure Deserialization (A08)
summary: Turning attacker bytes into objects can run their code (RCE). Fix: use JSON, never pickle/yaml on untrusted data.
objectives: See a payload execute during loads().
task: Which Python function running on untrusted data causes RCE? (one word, the module name)

title: Misconfig — Security Misconfiguration (A05)
summary: Cheap hardening most apps skip: security headers, generic errors, no debug mode.
objectives: Compare headers in vulnerable vs secure mode.
List the headers you now set by default.
task: Which response header (name) with value 'nosniff' stops MIME sniffing?

title: CTF — Capture a real flag
summary: Exploit a real IDOR and capture a flag, the way security people practise everywhere.
objectives: Find the FLAG in secret_note and submit it.
task: Exploit the IDOR (GET /api/account/3) and paste the FLAG{...}.
hint: Admin is id 3; flag is in secret_note.

title: API Security — OWASP API Top 10
summary: Modern apps are APIs with their own Top 10. #1 is Broken Object Level Authorization (the API's IDOR).
objectives: Spot BOLA and excessive data exposure.
task: OWASP API #1, Broken Object Level Authorization, is abbreviated ___ (4 letters).

title: AI/LLM — LLM Security
summary: OWASP Top 10 for LLM apps: prompt injection, insecure output handling, disclosure, excessive agency.
objectives: Watch each attack succeed then be blocked.
task: Tricking an LLM with 'ignore previous instructions' is called prompt ___ (one word).
hint: Same word as the SQL/command vuln family.

title: Threat Modeling — STRIDE
summary: Find design flaws early with STRIDE: Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information disclosure, Denial of service, Elevation of privilege.
task: Which STRIDE category is a forgeable 'admin:admin' token? (one word)

title: Code Review — Secure Code Review
summary: Reading code for the recurring sins: injection, secrets, verify=False, pickle, path traversal.
objectives: Study the sin patterns in the briefing.
Find each insecure branch and name the bug.
task: subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True) on user input is which injection? (two words)

title: SAST — Static Analysis
summary: SAST reads source (without running it) to flag risky patterns like input reaching a shell.
objectives: Read the vulnerability class it reports.
task: What vulnerability class does the SAST scanner report? (two words)

title: DAST — Dynamic Analysis
summary: DAST attacks the running app to confirm real exploitability (e.g. reflected XSS).
task: Attacking /greet with a <script> payload is which OWASP vuln? (3 letters)

title: SCA — Dependency Scanning
summary: Software Composition Analysis inventories dependencies and flags ones with known CVEs or no pinned version.
objectives: Learn how SCA uses an SBOM.
task: Scanning dependencies for known CVEs is called Software Composition Analysis, abbreviated ___ (3 letters).
hint: First letters of the three words.

title: Secrets — Secret Scanning
summary: Find committed credentials in code and git history; rotate anything ever committed.
task: Name a popular free tool that scans a repo for committed secrets (one word).

title: CI/CD — Pipeline Security
summary: A pipeline gate collects scanner findings and returns an exit code: 0 continues, non-zero blocks the build.
objectives: Run the gate on the samples with --fail-on HIGH.
Run echo $? to read the exit code.
task: What exit code does the gate return when it blocks the release? (a number)

title: IaC — Terraform Security
summary: Catch cloud misconfig in Terraform before apply: public S3, open SGs, public/unencrypted DBs, IAM wildcards.
objectives: Run iac-security-lab/scan.py on the insecure plan.
task: Scanning the insecure plan, which rule id fires for a publicly accessible database?

title: Containers — Docker Security
summary: Harden images: pin by digest, non-root user, minimal base, read-only fs, drop capabilities, scan for CVEs.
objectives: Compare insecure vs secure Dockerfile in container-k8s-lab.
task: A container should NOT run as which user? (one word)

title: Kubernetes — K8s Security
summary: Harden workloads to the restricted profile and enforce at admission with Kyverno/OPA.
objectives: Compare insecure vs secure Deployment in container-k8s-lab.
task: Which securityContext field must be true so a container does not run as root? (one word, no spaces)

title: Supply Chain — SBOM & Signing
summary: Know and trust your build: SBOM inventory, Cosign signing, SLSA provenance.
task: A machine-readable inventory of all components in your software is called an ___ (4-letter abbreviation).

title: Interview — Rs 70+ LPA prep
summary: Your infra background plus demonstrable AppSec+DevSecOps skill is the rare, high-paying combination.
objectives: Review what the senior band expects.
Pick two strongest as interview stories.
task: For a senior role, your strongest proof is a ___ of real projects (one word).
